paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. Paul is sitting in chains, and he is not complaining. He's THANKING God every time he remembers these believers (Philippians 1:3), and he prays with joy (Philippians 1:4). I think that tells us joy doesn't wait for a comfy kitchen.

Now the part I need you to hold onto. Paul is confident that "He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus" (Philippians 1:6). Who carries it? HE does. Not you, not me, not a baker with a stopwatch and a worried face. When my edges were worn and my stamps came out blurry, God was not done with me, and He's not done with you either.

So how do we grow while we wait? Paul prays that their love would "abound more and more in knowledge and depth of insight," so they can "test and prove what is best" (Philippians 1:9-10). Love and knowing the Word go together, friend. Then comes the finish line: "filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God" (Philippians 1:11). So keep showing up, keep learning, and let the glory go where Paul sends it.
